originalTitle: Analysis: Trump treats Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh as an ally. That creates economic risks
summary: Trump's reported phone calls to the Fed chairman will complicate his efforts to prove he will act independently on inflation and interest rates.
content:
After years of hostility toward the Federal Reserve , President Donald Trump has lately taken a new tack. He treats Chairman Kevin Warsh as almost a member of the Cabinet.

There is nothing in U.S. law that requires the Fed chairman to hang up if the president calls, and it is arguably beneficial for the nation's two most influential economic policymakers to understand where each is coming from.

But Trump's embrace of Warsh comes with risks for the economy . Fed independence isn't some abstract moral norm. It exists to protect politicians from their instincts to run the economy too hot and to give central bankers reason to be deliberate in how they exercise their tremendous power over the economy.

Trump has "spoken repeatedly" with Warsh since Warsh's confirmation as Fed chairman, The Wall Street Journal reported Wednesday . That marks a sharp change from the president's relationship with Warsh's predecessor Jerome Powell , whom Trump appointed and then soured on. Calendars published by the Fed show only one direct meeting between Trump and Powell during the president's second term through Warsh's swearing-in on May 22 — in addition to a messy episode when Powell and Trump toured a Fed construction site together.

Read more CNBC politics and policy coverage

The White House doesn't deny Trump and Warsh have spoken.

"President Trump has repeatedly stressed that he is giving Chairman Warsh the space he needs to restore confidence and competence in Fed decision-making," White House spokesman Kush Desai said in a statement. Trump respects Warsh's independence, Desai said.

Trump took legal steps to undermine the Fed's independence under Powell. And yet the president seems to have turned over a new leaf with Warsh's arrival. Trump hasn't dropped his demands that the Fed cut interest rates , but he has said repeatedly that he trusts Warsh.

The difference isn't policy but personnel. Trump was convinced that Powell was out to get him and was making interest-rate decisions to spite the president. Warsh can make the same decision — he hasn't changed the interest rates he inherited from Powell — and get a different result from Trump.

Warsh has other allies in the Trump administration. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent sharply criticized a Wall Street Journal reporter's coverage of the Fed in an X post Wednesday before the paper's story on the Trump-Warsh relationship ran. A Treasury spokeswoman didn't respond to questions about the post, but the upshot was clear. Here was the administration defending someone it sees as an ally against the hostile press.

The Fed declined to comment about the report that Trump has been calling Warsh. The chairman has said he's secure in his relationship with the president. He told the Senate last month he's willing to hear just about anyone with a point of view. "I certainly don't feel uncomfortable receiving a call from the chairman of this committee or the president of the United States," Warsh said . He will make his own decisions about interest rates.

A White House official said Thursday he wasn't party to the president's calls but believes the president is merely using Warsh as a sounding board, just like he does with other prominent people whose opinions he trusts. CNBC agreed to allow the official to speak anonymously to describe the president's thinking candidly. If Trump was pressuring Warsh to lower rates now, the world would know it, the official said. Trump would shout it from the rooftops, as he did with Powell. That hasn't happened.

But that doesn't mean Warsh can rest easy about Trump's decision to treat him as a kind of shadow Cabinet official.

Market commentators panned the chairman's performance at his second press conference last week. Warsh came out trying to give investors the impression he was on the edge of raising interest rates to fight inflation that has stayed above the Fed's 2% annual target for more than five years. But the chairman's answers to reporters' questions cast doubt on the more hawkish comments in his prepared remarks.

Investors sold off long-term-government debt as a hedge against the possibility that Warsh might not follow through on his pledge to take swift action against inflation.

The narrative that emerged was that Warsh had lost credibility. It isn't clear that's really the case. Market measures of inflation expectations, such as five-year inflation swaps, have fallen modestly since the Fed press conference, though they remain above 2%, according to LSEG data on Thursday afternoon. If inflation continues to ease, Warsh can keep rates on hold this year.

But should inflation spike and expectations rise, Trump will have put Warsh in a difficult position. He would need to demonstrate that he is willing to act. And that wouldn't come cheap, said Timothy Geithner , a former New York Fed president and treasury secretary under President Barack Obama.

"The risk is for the economy is that he'll have to do more than otherwise would be necessary to earn that credibility," Geithner said of Warsh on CNBC Tuesday. Higher interest rates tend to slow the economy. Slowing the economy to prove a political point is the last thing a Fed chair should do.

It would also be self-defeating for Trump, who won the presidency again in 2024 after inflation crippled President Joe Biden's administration.

A congressman pointed out the irony to Warsh at a hearing last month. "Had your predecessor caved to Trump, and lowered interest rates below what economics would call for, we would have much higher inflation today," Rep. Brad Sherman, D-Calif., told Warsh. Republicans' would have taken a political hit, he said. "Your agency has saved Donald Trump from himself," Sherman said.

Warsh didn't reply, but for a moment, he cracked a smile.
chineseTitle: 分析：特朗普将美联储主席凯文·沃什视为盟友。这会带来经济风险
chineseSummary: 据报道，特朗普给美联储主席的电话将使他证明自己将在通胀和利率问题上独立采取行动的努力变得更加复杂。
chineseContent:
经过多年对美联储的敌意后，唐纳德·特朗普总统最近采取了新的策略。他几乎将董事长凯文·沃什视为内阁成员。

美国法律中并没有规定美联储主席在总统打电话时必须挂断电话，而且对于美国两位最有影响力的经济政策制定者来说，了解彼此的想法可能是有益的。

但特朗普对沃什的拥抱也给经济带来了风险。美联储的独立性并不是某种抽象的道德规范。它的存在是为了保护政客免受经济过热的本能的影响，并让央行行长有理由深思熟虑如何行使对经济的巨大权力。

据《华尔街日报》周三报道，自沃什被确认担任美联储主席以来，特朗普与沃什“多次交谈”。这标志着总统与沃什的前任杰罗姆·鲍威尔的关系发生了巨大变化，鲍威尔是特朗普任命的，但后来又对其产生了不满。美联储公布的日历显示，特朗普和鲍威尔在总统第二任期至沃什 5 月 22 日宣誓就职期间只进行过一次直接会面，此外还有鲍威尔和特朗普一起参观美联储建筑工地时发生的混乱事件。

阅读更多 CNBC 政治和政策报道

白宫并不否认特朗普和沃什的谈话。

白宫发言人库什·德赛在一份声明中表示，“特朗普总统一再强调，他正在给予沃什主席所需的空间，以恢复对美联储决策的信心和能力。”德赛说，特朗普尊重沃什的独立性。

特朗普采取法律措施破坏鲍威尔领导下的美联储独立性。然而，随着沃什的到来，总统似乎已经翻开了新的一页。特朗普并没有放弃对美联储降息的要求，但他多次表示他信任沃什。

区别不在于政策，而在于人员。特朗普确信鲍威尔是想抓他，并做出利率决定来激怒总统。沃什可以做出同样的决定——他没有改变从鲍威尔那里继承的利率——并得到与特朗普不同的结果。

沃什在特朗普政府中还有其他盟友。周三，在《华尔街日报》关于特朗普与沃什关系的报道发表之前，美国财政部长斯科特·贝森特 (Scott Bessent) 在 X 帖子中严厉批评了《华尔街日报》记者对美联储的报道。财政部发言人没有回应有关该帖子的问题，但结果很明显。这是政府在为它视为盟友的人辩护，对抗敌对媒体。

美联储拒绝对特朗普一直称沃什的报道发表评论。主席表示他与总统的关系是安全的。他上个月告诉参议院，他愿意听取任何有观点的人的意见。 “接到委员会主席或美国总统的电话我当然不会感到不舒服，”沃什说。他将自行决定利率。

一名白宫官员周四表示，他并未参与总统的呼吁，但认为总统只是利用沃什作为参谋，就像他对其他他信任其观点的知名人士所做的那样。 CNBC 同意允许该官员匿名发言，以坦诚地描述总统的想法。这位官员表示，如果特朗普现在向沃什施压要求降低利率，全世界都会知道。特朗普会在屋顶上大声喊叫，就像他对鲍威尔所做的那样。那还没有发生。

但这并不意味着沃什可以对特朗普将他视为影子内阁官员的决定高枕无忧。

市场评论员批评了董事长上周第二次新闻发布会上的表现。沃什试图给投资者留下这样的印象：他正处于加息的边缘，以应对五年多来一直高于美联储2%年度目标的通胀。但主席对记者提问的回答让人对他准备好的讲话中更为鹰派的言论产生了怀疑。

投资者抛售长期政府债务，以对冲沃什可能无法兑现其迅速采取行动应对通胀的承诺。

出现的说法是沃什已经失去了可信度。目前还不清楚情况是否真的如此。伦敦证券交易所集团周四下午的数据显示，自美联储新闻发布会以来，衡量通胀预期的市场指标（例如五年期通胀掉期）已小幅下降，但仍保持在 2% 以上。如果通胀继续缓解，沃什今年可能会维持利率不变。

但如果通胀飙升、预期上升，特朗普就会让沃什陷入困境。他需要证明他愿意采取行动。前纽约联邦储备银行行长、巴拉克·奥巴马总统时期的财政部长蒂莫西·盖特纳表示，这并不便宜。

周二，盖特纳在接受 CNBC 采访时谈到沃什时表示：“经济面临的风险是，他必须做更多的事情来赢得信誉。”较高的利率往往会导致经济放缓。为了证明政治观点而放慢经济增长是美联储主席最不应该做的事情。

对于特朗普来说，这也将是弄巧成拙的，他在通胀削弱了乔·拜登总统的政府后，于 2024 年再次赢得了总统宝座。

一名国会议员在上个月的一次听证会上向沃什指出了这一讽刺。加利福尼亚州民主党众议员布拉德·谢尔曼 (Brad Sherman) 告诉沃什：“如果你的前任屈服于特朗普，并将利率降低到经济要求以下，我们今天的通胀率将会高得多。”他说，共和党人会受到政治打击。 “你们的机构把唐纳德·特朗普从自己手中救了出来，”谢尔曼说。

沃什没有回答，但片刻他露出了笑容。
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于财经市场信号，适合用于观察利率、汇率、股债商品、金融机构和宏观政策变化。
